newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Heavy crudes strong, Oman rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Heavy crudes strong, Oman rebounds.

text.p: Sentiment on the heavy Asian crude market was bullish although August activity will only pick up next week, traders said on Wednesday.
August Minas was offered at ICP +70/80 cents per barrel, with bids expected to come from ICP +50/60.
This compared with recent July Minas parcels traded around ICP +50.
West African cargoes trading to Asian refiners have resumed, despite a wider Brent/Dubai spread, with a U.S. major buying an August loading cargo, probably to supply South Korea.
Details of the trade was not revealed.
But widespread rumours that the purchase was for an August 10-20 cargo of Qua Iboe was denied by the major.
Traders said that there was limited interest from most Asian refiners for West African cargoes because of the widening Brent/Dubai spread.
A Brent/Dubai differential of under $1.00 is seen as the workable spread for West African cargoes to come East.

August Brent/Dubai was quoted at $1.12/$1.17 on Wednesday. But traders also said Korean buyers were less concerned about the spread as West African crudes were increasingly becoming their baseload supply due to the size of the cargoes.
In the Mideast market, prices have rebounded slightly as the last August cargoes find homes.
Oman was traded at Dubai +1 and +2 to Korea and a US major.
This is firmer than Oman deals done end last week at Dubai -10 and Dubai -3.
The last Abu Dhabi crude supplies were also slowly getting placed, leaving traders optimistic that the overhang seen in the June and July market will not be repeated in August.
"It's not bullish, but I'm a bit more relaxed than I was in June" said a western trader.
